definition: Transferring reasoning behaviour from a stronger model into a smaller one by training on its traces or its preferences. The sources use it for three targets and one of them revises how it should be done. The original demonstration distils long chain-of-thought from an RL-trained reasoning model into smaller checkpoints. One distils verification rather than problem-solving, producing a 4B guardrail that beats 7B and 8B specialists and GPT-4o at judging groundedness. One argues the transferred structure must match the student's capacity rather than the teacher's, pruning by mathematical skill before distilling, and cuts GSM8K tokens from 917 to 328 while raising accuracy from 91.7% to 94.1%.

evidence.note: Shows that reasoning ability can be incentivized in an LLM by pure reinforcement learning on verifiable tasks, with no human-annotated reasoning trajectories, and that the resulting reasoning patterns can be transferred to smaller models.
evidence.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning

evidence.note: Has a teacher decompose and prune a student's reasoning by mathematical skill, then distills the pruned paths back, on the argument that CoT structure must match student capacity.
evidence.title: DRP: Distilled Reasoning Pruning with Mathematical Skill-aware Step Decomposition for Efficient Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: A 4B small reasoning model that classifies document-claim pairs as grounded or hallucinated for RAG pipelines and produces evidence-grounded justifications.
evidence.title: HalluGuard: Evidence-Grounded Small Reasoning Models to Mitigate Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

evidence.note: Finds that the </think> token aggregates the reasoning chain in deep layers and that attention paid to it from that position ranks which steps matter, then uses that ranking to drive a four-operator compression search — cutting 58% of tokens with accuracy holding.
evidence.title: CRISP: Compressing Redundancy in Chain-of-Thought via Intrinsic Saliency Pruning

evidence.note: Runs the head-to-head this literature had been missing, comparing three importance criteria on the same traces at matched compression ratios, and finds step-level criteria agree on what to keep while disagreeing on what to cut — because redundancy is diffuse rather than located in any identifiable class of step.
evidence.title: When Compression Helps and When It Hurts: Condition-Aware Analysis of Chain-of-Thought Distillation

evidence.note: Measures RLVR-trained models against their base models with pass@k at large k and finds the base wins, concluding RLVR sharpens sampling toward paths the base already had rather than adding new ones.
evidence.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?

evidence.note: Reads a reasoning trajectory as a multi-step pseudo-gradient descent on the model's own parameters, which makes each token an optimization step, the trajectory an inner loop, and the training regime a meta-learning problem in which the question is the task.
evidence.title: Deciphering Trajectory-Aided LLM Reasoning: An Optimization Perspective

name: reasoning distillation
